questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.hint: It is a planned city. An American architect drew the plan for it in 1911 and 1912, and it got its name in 1913.
questions.explanation: Canberra was built to be the capital. Parliament chose the site in 1908 and met in Melbourne until it moved to the new city in 1927. Sydney and Melbourne are much larger, but neither is the capital.

image.alt: An old plan of a city with wide avenues, circles and a winding river, drawn in ink on a survey map.

label.title: Competition plan for the federal capital of Australia, later named Canberra

sources.label: Parliamentary Education Office, Australian Parliament history timeline

questions.question: Which is the highest mountain in Africa?
questions.hint: It is an old volcano with three peaks. It stands alone, not in a mountain range, and its ice is shrinking.
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania and rises to 5,895 metres. It still has ice at the top, although it lies close to the equator. Mount Kenya is the second highest mountain in Africa, at 5,199 metres.

image.alt: A broad mountain seen from above, with a white cap of snow and a round crater at the top, and dark forest around it.

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania

questions.question: To which country do the Azores islands belong?
questions.hint: The islands lie about 1,400 km west of this country's mainland. Their largest town is Ponta Delgada.
questions.explanation: The Azores are nine volcanic islands in the middle of the North Atlantic. They are an autonomous region of Portugal. Portugal has one more autonomous region, and it is also a group of Atlantic islands: Madeira.

image.alt: Seven green islands of different shapes scattered over a dark ocean, seen from space.

label.artist: NASA (Jeff Schmaltz, MODIS Rapid Response Team)
label.title: The Azores seen from the Terra satellite

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, São Miguel, Azores

questions.question: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?
options: The Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Red Sea and the Arabian Sea
The Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea
questions.hint: The canal crosses Egypt from Port Said in the north to the city of Suez in the south.
questions.explanation: The canal opened in November 1869 after ten years of work, and it is about 193 km long. Ships sailing between Europe and Asia can use it and do not have to go around Africa.

image.alt: A thin dark line of water runs from a sea at the top to another sea at the bottom, through yellow desert and past green fields.

label.title: The Suez Canal from space (NASA World Wind, Landsat images)

sources.label: Suez Canal Authority, About the Suez Canal
NASA Earth Observatory, The New Suez Canal

questions.question: Which strait connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara?
questions.hint: A very large city stands on both of its shores, partly in Europe and partly in Asia.
questions.explanation: The Bosporus runs through Istanbul and is part of the border between Europe and Asia. The Dardanelles are at the other end of the Sea of Marmara and lead to the Aegean Sea. Together they are called the Turkish Straits.

image.alt: A narrow, winding channel of pale water joins two dark seas, with a large pink-grey city on both banks.

label.title: Istanbul and the Bosporus from the International Space Station

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Bosporus Strait and Istanbul, Turkey

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.hint: It is a rift lake, long and narrow. It is also the oldest lake in the world, at about 25 million years.
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is more than 1,600 metres deep. It holds more than a fifth of the fresh water on the Earth's surface, more than all the Great Lakes of North America together. Lake Tanganyika, in Africa, is the second deepest.

image.alt: A long, curved, dark lake seen from space, with snow on the mountains around it.

label.artist: NASA (Jacques Descloitres, MODIS Land Rapid Response Team)
label.title: Lake Baikal from the Terra satellite

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Melting Ice on Lake Baikal

questions.question: Which is the longest river in Europe?
questions.hint: It never reaches the open ocean. It ends in a wide delta on the shore of an inland sea.
questions.explanation: The Volga flows for more than 3,500 km through Russia and ends in the Caspian Sea. Its delta is the largest in Europe. The Danube, which ends in the Black Sea, is the second longest river in Europe.

image.alt: A river splits into hundreds of small channels in a green, fan-shaped delta, seen from space.

label.title: The Volga Delta from the International Space Station

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Volga River Delta

questions.question: Counting polar deserts, on which continent is the largest desert on Earth?
questions.hint: A desert is a place with very little rain or snow. It does not have to be hot or sandy.
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the driest continent. So little snow falls there that almost all of it counts as a desert, of about 14 million square kilometres. The Sahara, in Africa, is the largest hot desert, at about 9 million square kilometres.

image.alt: A wide, empty valley of grey stones and bare brown mountains under a blue sky.

label.title: Wright Valley, Antarctica, seen from the foot of Bull Pass
label.place: Wikimedia Commons (released into the public domain by the photographer)

questions.question: Which is the largest country in Africa by area?
questions.hint: Its capital is on the Mediterranean coast, but the Sahara covers most of the country.
questions.explanation: Algeria covers about 2.38 million square kilometres. Sudan was the largest country in Africa until 2011, when its southern part became a new country, South Sudan. The Democratic Republic of the Congo is now the second largest.

image.alt: Africa seen from space, with pale desert in the north and dark green forest in the centre.

sources.label: Wikipedia, List of African countries by area

questions.question: A doubly landlocked country has no sea coast, and all its neighbours are landlocked too. Only two exist. One is Uzbekistan. Which is the other?
questions.hint: Its capital is Vaduz, and its head of state is a prince.
questions.explanation: Liechtenstein lies between Switzerland and Austria, and neither has a sea coast. Uzbekistan has five neighbours, all landlocked. From either country you must cross at least two borders to reach the ocean.

image.alt: A political map of Central Asia and the Caucasus, with each country in a different colour.
